title: Synthetic canary scheduler and graded circuit weave for autoscale stability
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We observe autoscaler thrashing and cascading regional failovers when probe fanout spikes during region pressure events. Existing readiness/liveness probes are synchronous and often cause many replicas to be marked unready simultaneously, prompting scale-down/up cycles that violate SLOs. This ticket builds a two-pronged mitigation: (1) a synthetic canary scheduler that staggers and shapes health probes and lightweight synthetic transactions to reduce fanout and provide early localized signals, and (2) a graded "circuit weave" policy that blends per-region circuit breakers with token-weighted request-contract enforcement so that load shedding is proportional, predictable, and SLO-aware.
proposal: Implement a synthetic canary scheduler service (distributed, region-aware) to issue configurable synthetic transactions and stagger probe windows with jitter and localized cooling. Add a graded circuit-weave controller that composes: per-region circuit scores (latency/error budgets), per-route token-weighted admission control, and a soft-fallback matrix mapping degraded states to allowed request cohorts (interactive vs background). Integrate scheduler outputs into autoscaler decision inputs as a separate stability signal with hysteresis and decay.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic scheduler can run in each region and produce staggered synthetic transactions for 80% of routes without increasing total probe volume
Autoscaler uses synthetic-stability-signal and reduces scale thrash metrics (scale events/min) by >= 60% in the staging failure simulation
Graded circuit-weave applies token-weighted shedding and limits tail-QPS for interactive routes during degraded windows with <1% request rejection for high-tier customers
End-to-end playbook documented and tested: failover walkthrough, manual override, and rollback steps
Load-shedding decisions are logged and visible in Console per-token and per-route with links to the circuit state
plan: Spike: design synthetic transaction shape and low-overhead instrumentation (2 days)
Implement scheduler prototype that supports jittered windows and region affinity (3 days)
Add synthetic-stability-signal pipeline to telemetry and autoscaler inputs (2 days)
Implement circuit-weave controller with token-weighted gates and degradation matrix (5 days)
Run chaos+load simulations in staging, tune hysteresis and decay windows (3 days)
Rollout canary to a non-critical cluster, monitor for 48h, then expand (2 days)
Postmortem and tuning: update playbook and dashboarding (1 day)
rollout_steps: Feature flag synthetic scheduler and circuit-weave off by default
Enable synthetic scheduler in staging for a subset (~10%) of routes
Feed synthetic-stability-signal into autoscaler in observe-only mode for 24h
Enable circuit-weave soft-enforcement (logging + simulated shed decisions) for 24h
Enable soft-enforcement in production for low-traffic clusters with rapid rollback
Gradually increase coverage and tighten enforcement windows while monitoring SLOs
test_plan: Unit tests for scheduler timing, jitter, and region affinity
Integration test: synthetic signal reaches autoscaler and is applied as stability input
Staging chaos test: simulate regional latency spike + pod OOM and assert no >2x increase in scale events
SLO regression test: run representative workload and ensure P95 latency and error budget remain within target
Observability test: circuit state and shed logs are queryable in Console and match expected decisions
risks_mitigation: Synthetic traffic could add load: keep synthetic QPS <1% of baseline and cap per-region concurrency
False-positive degradation from synthetic transaction: use ensemble of signals (synthetic + real traffic metrics)
Complexity of circuit-weave logic: start with simple graded thresholds and expand with telemetry
Monitoring blind spots: add explicit dashboards and alerts for synthetic scheduler health
dependencies_notes: Requires telemetry ingestion change (downstream schema) and Console dashboard tile. Coordinate with infra telemetry team and Console owners. See design doc linked below.
